verdicts.reason: A flips the original order (book left, text right), and the beige circle sits alone at the far right, cut off from the book it used to back, leaving dead space on both sides. B has the same split circle, and its book cover is jammed against the left and top edges with almost no margin. B's larger headline does not make up for the cramped corner.

B keeps the original reading order (headline and copy on the left, book on the right) with a strong, legible headline. But the circle is still a separate blob at the far right instead of sitting behind the book, and the book floats in the middle. A reverses the order, has a large empty left margin, smaller type, and the same orphaned circle.

B is the only layout that keeps the book layered on the beige circle as in the original, with the text on the left, so it is the most faithful. However, the book is crammed against the right, top and bottom edges, and there is a wide empty gap between the copy and the book. A reverses the order, cuts the circle off from the book, and leaves uneven dead space at both ends.
